key_insight: Weekly blood microsampling detected elevated interferon-related transcriptomic signals before and during dermatomyositis flares.
clinical_relevance: This suggests a minimally invasive way to monitor flare risk longitudinally in dermatomyositis, potentially helping clinicians identify worsening disease earlier.
method: 6-month feasibility study in 6 women with inactive or minimally active dermatomyositis
Patients self-reported weekly PtGA scores; flare defined as PtGA increase >2 for 2 consecutive weeks
Weekly 125 µL blood microsamples were shipped for RNA sequencing and bioinformatic analysis
evidence_signal: Among 54 sequenced samples across 9 timepoints, interferon scores were significantly higher in flare-associated samples, with enrichment of interferon-related gene sets in pre-flare and flare periods.
watch_item: Findings are preliminary and based on a very small single-study cohort, so performance for routine flare prediction still needs larger validation.
paper_title: Longitudinal interferon signatures are associated with disease flare in dermatomyositis
